verification.notes: Checked the May 27 signed rule and named exceptions, narrow medical permissions and later mixed enforcement observations; no continuous all-traffic closure is claimed.

summary: The Gambia announced a ban on live poultry, chicken meat and eggs from Senegal and other affected origins on 15 January 2021 following avian influenza outbreaks. Imports from unaffected countries remained permitted. Reporting in August still described restrictions on chicks, but no matching lifting notice was established. The measure targeted specified animal products and origins rather than passengers or all goods crossing the land frontier.

verification.notes: Verified January 15 announcement, affected poultry products/origins and later continuing chick restriction, with unaffected imports and unknown lifting retained.

summary: Mali suspended exports of millet, sorghum, maize, local rice, cottonseed and cottonseed cake from 6 December 2021 to protect domestic food supplies and prices. The ministry still described the order as in force in May 2023. Later reporting referred to lifting restrictions for Niger as a solidarity measure, but did not establish the full commodity coverage or repeal date. The rule concerned outward shipments of listed products, not all border traffic.

verification.notes: Confirmed December 6 commodity list and ministry’s May 2023 continuation, while the later Niger solidarity lifting lacks complete product scope or an exact repeal.

summary: Burkina Faso restricted cereal exports to protect domestic supplies and prices, suspending new permits from January 2021 and later prohibiting use of existing permits for named crops. Separate measures covered millet, maize and sorghum flour from 2022, while later grain notices also named rice and cowpea. Limited Niger-bound exports received exceptional permission in 2023. Flour restrictions were lifted in July 2026 with permits still required, then renewed in October; these changing commodity rules did not close the border to all trade.

verification.notes: Checked January 2021 permit suspension, later grain/flour distinctions and Niger exception; July lifting and October 2026 renewed flour rule remain separate phases.

summary: Ghana instructed customs stations at Tatale, Wonjuga, Bunkpurugu and Saboba to prevent grain and soybean exports in late 2022 to protect domestic supplies. A separate national announcement on 26 August 2024 restricted grain exports, explicitly including corn and rice, amid food-security concerns. Later reports described continuing enforcement, but did not establish an exact repeal or traffic conditions at every post. Export licensing requirements alone are not treated as proof that every shipment was prohibited.

verification.notes: Verified four-station 2022 directive separately from August 2024 national grain restriction and later enforcement, without equating ordinary licensing law with a universal prohibition.

summary: Burkina Faso announced restrictions on imports of poultry and avian products from Benin, Togo and Côte d’Ivoire on 20 August 2021 in response to avian influenza. The ministry called for stronger border controls on those products and origins. The announcement does not establish the first rejected shipment or a subsequent lifting date. It did not amount to a ban on unaffected countries’ products, unrelated cargo or ordinary travellers.

verification.notes: Checked the Friday August 20 ministry announcement, three origins and avian-influenza purpose; no shipment-level start, repeal or unrelated-traffic ban is inferred.

summary: Sudanese authorities withdrew permission for humanitarian truck consignments to enter Darfur through Adré from Chad on 21 February 2024, citing alleged weapons movements. Some convoys received exceptional permission in March and April, and Tine remained a separately authorised route. General permission for Adré aid movements returned on 15–16 August, followed by a WFP food convoy on 20 August. The intervening exceptions mean this was not a continuous period with no aid entering.

verification.notes: Verified February 21 permission withdrawal, exceptional March/April convoys and Tine route, then August 15–16 permission followed by actual August 20 WFP entry.
